      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: we generated zebrafish myelin regulatory factor (myrf) mutants with CNS-specific hypomyelination and investigated how this affected their axonal conduction properties and behavior.
      explanation: >-
        States the genotype and what the study set out to measure in it.
  notes: >-
    Added from the alternative-models deep research run for this entry. Paired
    with the Tg(mbp:mCherry-NTR) ablation line on the same node and
    deliberately kept separate from it: that line removes established myelin
    and recovers, this one never builds it, and the two answer different
    halves of the node.
- name: Glucocorticoid receptor (gr) loss-of-function zebrafish
  species: Danio rerio
  genotype: Adult-viable gr mutant in which all transcriptional activity of the glucocorticoid receptor is abolished, so cortisol rises but cannot signal through GR. The allele is not named in the abstract.
  category: Genetic loss-of-function model of glucocorticoid negative feedback
  publication: PMID:22641177
  description: >-
    A zebrafish mutant that survives to adulthood with no GR transcriptional
    activity. Negative feedback on the stress axis is lost and cortisol is
    elevated but inert at GR. In an unfamiliar tank the mutants freeze, explore
    less and fail to habituate on repeated exposure. Fluoxetine in the holding
    water, and social interaction, restore the behaviour, with cortisol
    correcting later; fluoxetine does not change baseline transcription of CRH,
    MR, the serotonin transporter or GR, but suppresses their stress-induced
    upregulation. The authors offer it as a platform for high-throughput
    antidepressant screening.
  associated_phenotypes:
  - Loss of negative feedback on the stress response
  - Elevated cortisol
  - Freezing and reduced exploration in a novel tank
  - Failure to habituate to a repeated stressor
  - Behavioural rescue by fluoxetine and by social interaction
  modeled_mechanisms:
  - target: HPA Axis Dysregulation
    relationship: PARTIALLY_RECAPITULATES
    fidelity: LOW
    model_scale: ORGANISM
    description: >-
      Produces the node's elevated-cortisol state and ties it to a persistent,
      non-habituating behavioural phenotype that antidepressant treatment
      reverses. The teleost hypothalamic-pituitary-interrenal axis is the
      homologue of the mammalian HPA axis, and the receptor the node's
      mechanism runs through is the one disrupted.
    limitations: >-
      Cortisol is elevated here because feedback is broken at the receptor, so
      no tissue can respond to it. The node describes axis hyperactivity with
      receptor signalling intact, which is a different state: the mutant
      cannot show glucocorticoid-driven hippocampal atrophy, because the
      glucocorticoid cannot act. The hippocampal-atrophy and cognitive arms of
      the node are therefore out of reach, and the fish has no hippocampus
      proper.
    divergences:
    - divergence_type: CONTESTED_ASSUMPTION
      description: >-
        The node's mechanism is elevated cortisol acting on tissue. In this
        model cortisol is elevated precisely because it cannot act. Readouts
        downstream of GR occupancy are not merely attenuated but absent, so
        the model inverts the node's causal step while reproducing its
        headline measurement.
      materiality: INVALIDATING
    - divergence_type: SPECIES_MISMATCH
      description: >-
        Teleost; the stress axis is the hypothalamic-pituitary-interrenal
        axis, cortisol is the glucocorticoid as in humans, but there is no
        adrenal cortex and no hippocampus in the mammalian sense, which is the
        structure the node's downstream claim concerns.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    readouts:
    - name: Whole-animal cortisol
      target: HPA Axis Dysregulation
      direction: INCREASED
      interpretation: >-
        Reproduces the node's elevated-glucocorticoid state, but as a
        consequence of abolished receptor signalling rather than of axis drive.
      evidence:
      - reference: PMID:22641177
        reference_title: An affective disorder in zebrafish with mutation of the glucocorticoid receptor.
        supports: SUPPORT
        evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
        directness: DIRECT
        quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
        snippet: As a consequence, cortisol is elevated, but unable to signal through GR.
        explanation: >-
          States both the shared measurement and the divergence from the node
          in one sentence.
    - name: Novel tank freezing, exploration and habituation
      target: HPA Axis Dysregulation
      direction: ALTERED
      interpretation: >-
        Behavioural consequence of disrupted glucocorticoid feedback,
        reversible by fluoxetine. A stress-response phenotype, not a
        diagnosis-equivalent measure.
      evidence:
      - reference: PMID:22641177
        reference_title: An affective disorder in zebrafish with mutation of the glucocorticoid receptor.
        supports: SUPPORT
        evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
        directness: INDIRECT
        quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
        snippet: When placed into an unfamiliar aquarium ('novel tank'), mutant fish become immobile ('freeze'), show reduced exploratory behavior and do not habituate to this stressor upon repeated exposure.
        explanation: >-
          The behavioural phenotype, including the failure to habituate, which
          is what distinguishes it from an acute stress response.
      - reference: PMID:22641177
        reference_title: An affective disorder in zebrafish with mutation of the glucocorticoid receptor.
        supports: SUPPORT
        evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
        directness: INDIRECT
        quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
        snippet: Addition of the antidepressant fluoxetine to the holding water and social interactions restore normal behavior, followed by a delayed correction of cortisol levels.
        explanation: >-
          Pharmacological reversal, and the order of recovery: behaviour
          first, cortisol after.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:22641177
      reference_title: An affective disorder in zebrafish with mutation of the glucocorticoid receptor.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: We identified an adult-viable zebrafish mutant in which the negative feedback on the stress response is disrupted, due to abolition of all transcriptional activity of GR.
      explanation: >-
        Defines the genotype and the lesion in the stress axis.
    - reference: PMID:22641177
      reference_title: An affective disorder in zebrafish with mutation of the glucocorticoid receptor.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      snippet: Dysregulation of the stress axis is a hallmark of major depression in human patients.
      explanation: >-
        The authors' own statement of why the axis is the target. Background,
        not a result of this model.
  notes: >-
    Added from the alternative-models deep research run for this entry. This
    node is not one of the five the run focused on; the candidate was returned
    alongside them and is included because the node had no model linked to it
    and the mechanism is a receptor-level match. The INVALIDATING divergence is
    the point of the record: the model shares the node's measurement and
    reverses its causal direction, so it should not be read as a
    hypercortisolism model.
- name: Adult zebrafish chronic unpredictable stress, 5 and 12 weeks
  species: Danio rerio
  genotype: Wild-type adult zebrafish; no genetic manipulation
  category: Chronic stress exposure model
  publication: PMID:40220038
  description: >-
    Adult zebrafish exposed to five or twelve weeks of chronic unpredictable
    stress, assayed for behaviour, whole-body cortisol, brain monoamines,
    blood-brain-barrier permeability and a panel of pro- and
    anti-inflammatory microglial and astroglial marker genes. The two
    durations dissociate: five weeks produced anxiety-like behaviour with
    raised pro-inflammatory markers, cortisol signalling and norepinephrine,
    while twelve weeks produced depression-like behaviour with lowered
    cortisol, impaired serotonin turnover and activation of
    anti-inflammatory markers instead.
  associated_phenotypes:
  - Anxiety-like behaviour after five weeks
  - Depression-like behaviour after twelve weeks
  - Elevated pro-inflammatory microglial and astroglial marker expression after five weeks
  - Activated anti-inflammatory marker expression after twelve weeks
  - Lowered cortisol after twelve weeks
  - Impaired serotonin turnover after twelve weeks
  modeled_mechanisms:
  - target: Neuroinflammation
    relationship: PARTIALLY_RECAPITULATES
    fidelity: LOW
    model_scale: ORGANISM
    description: >-
      Puts glial inflammatory marker expression, stress duration and affective
      behaviour on the same axis in one experiment, which is what the node
      asserts a relationship between. Its result partly contradicts the node:
      the pro-inflammatory profile travelled with the anxiety-like
      five-week state, and the depression-like twelve-week state came with
      anti-inflammatory markers and lowered cortisol.
    limitations: >-
      The readouts are marker gene expression in whole brain, not cytokine
      protein in the cell types the node names, and the node's human markers
      (IL-6, TNF-alpha, CRP) are not among them. Behaviour is scored on
      zebrafish anxiety and depression-like assays. The dissociation between
      stress duration and inflammatory polarity is a single-study result and
      is recorded here as such.
    divergences:
    - divergence_type: CONTESTED_ASSUMPTION
      description: >-
        The node states that elevated inflammatory cytokines are observed in
        depression. In this model the depression-like phase was accompanied by
        activated anti-inflammatory rather than pro-inflammatory markers, with
        the pro-inflammatory profile belonging to the earlier anxiety-like
        phase. The model therefore qualifies the node's direction rather than
        confirming it.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    - divergence_type: PROXY_QUANTITY
      description: >-
        Pro- and anti-inflammatory state is inferred from a marker gene panel
        (NOS2a, COX2, P75NTR, C3, GBP against ARG-1, CD206, S100a10, PTX), not
        from the cytokines the node names.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    - divergence_type: TEMPORAL_SCOPE
      description: >-
        The finding is specifically about stress duration, five weeks against
        twelve. The node is not time-resolved, so a model whose result depends
        on duration cannot be mapped onto it without choosing a timepoint.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    readouts:
    - name: CNS pro-inflammatory glial marker gene expression after five weeks
      target: Neuroinflammation
      direction: INCREASED
      interpretation: >-
        The node's direction, but in the anxiety-like rather than the
        depression-like state.
      evidence:
      - reference: PMID:40220038
        reference_title: Prolonged 5-week and 12-week chronic stress differentially modulates CNS expression of pro- and anti-neuroinflammatory biomarkers, brain monoamines and affective behavior in adult zebrafish.
        supports: SUPPORT
        evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
        directness: INDIRECT
        quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
        snippet: Overall, CUS5 induced anxiety-like behavior, accompanied by elevated CNS pro-inflammatory marker gene expression, cortisol signaling and norepinephrine levels.
        explanation: >-
          The five-week result, which pairs the node's inflammatory direction
          with anxiety rather than depression.
    - name: CNS anti-inflammatory glial marker gene expression after twelve weeks
      target: Neuroinflammation
      direction: INCREASED
      interpretation: >-
        Opposite polarity to the node, in the state the authors read as
        depression-like. Recorded because it constrains how this model may be
        cited for the node.
      evidence:
      - reference: PMID:40220038
        reference_title: Prolonged 5-week and 12-week chronic stress differentially modulates CNS expression of pro- and anti-neuroinflammatory biomarkers, brain monoamines and affective behavior in adult zebrafish.
        supports: REFUTE
        evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
        directness: INDIRECT
        quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
        snippet: In contrast, CUS12 induced depression-like behavior, accompanied by lowered cortisol levels, impaired serotonin turnover and activated anti-inflammatory biomarker gene expression, as well as upregulated histone deacetylase 4 gene (suggesting the involvement of epigenetic regulation).
        explanation: >-
          The twelve-week result. Marked REFUTE against the node's stated
          direction, not against the existence of a stress-inflammation link.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:40220038
      reference_title: Prolonged 5-week and 12-week chronic stress differentially modulates CNS expression of pro- and anti-neuroinflammatory biomarkers, brain monoamines and affective behavior in adult zebrafish.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: Here, we examined the effects of 5- and 12-week chronic unpredictable stress (CUS5 and CUS12) on zebrafish behavior, whole-body cortisol and neuroinflammation-related biomarker gene expression, including markers of pro-inflammatory microglia (NOS2a, COX2, P75NTR) and astroglia (C3, GBP), and markers of anti-inflammatory microglia (ARG-1, CD206) and astroglia (S100a10, PTX).
      explanation: >-
        The design and the full marker panel, which is what the readouts rest
        on.
  notes: >-
    Added from the alternative-models deep research run for this entry.
    Neuroinflammation was the only one of the run's five focus nodes that
    already had models linked, all of them mouse; this adds a non-mammalian
    one whose result does not simply agree with them. The duration-dependent
    reversal of inflammatory polarity is worth revisiting if the node is ever
    split by illness stage.

experimental_models:
- name: iPSC-derived microglia-like cells under diverse inflammogens
  experimental_model_type: IPSC_DERIVED_MODEL
  organism:
    preferred_term: Homo sapiens
    term:
      id: NCBITaxon:9606
      label: Homo sapiens
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: Microglia-like cell
    term:
      id: CL:0000129
      label: microglial cell
  cell_source: Human induced pluripotent stem cells
  culture_system: Microglia-like cell monoculture, with conditioned-medium transfer onto astrocytes for the crosstalk assay
  conditions:
  - Unstimulated
  - TNF-alpha
  - Interferon-gamma
  - FSL-1 (TLR2)
  - Poly(I:C) (TLR3)
  - Lipopolysaccharide (TLR4)
  - Imiquimod (TLR7)
  publication: PMID:41227333
  description: >-
    Microglia-like cells differentiated from human iPSCs, validated by
    transcriptome profiling against microglial signature genes, then mapped
    across inflammatory states by stimulating them with cytokines and with
    agonists of four Toll-like receptors. Each stimulus gave a distinguishable
    morphology, cytokine secretion profile and transcriptional signature, and
    engaged NF-kB or JAK-STAT signalling selectively. Supernatants from
    microglia stimulated with FSL-1, LPS or Poly(I:C) activated astrocytes, and
    that propagation was strictly dependent on TNF-alpha.
  modeled_mechanisms:
  - target: Neuroinflammation
    relationship: MEASURES
    fidelity: MODERATE
    model_scale: CELLULAR
    description: >-
      Supplies a human-cell assay for the activation state of the cell type
      the node names, and resolves it by stimulus rather than treating
      activation as one condition. The microglia-to-astrocyte arm addresses the
      same crosstalk that the entry's P2rx7/Il6/Il6ra mouse model proposes,
      in human cells and with a different mediator.
    limitations: >-
      Monoculture of one cell type, with astrocytes reached only through
      transferred medium; no neurons, no vasculature, no tissue context. The
      stimuli are pathogen-associated or cytokine challenges, not the chronic
      stress the node's upstream causes imply, and nothing links any state to
      an affective outcome. iPSC-derived microglia-like cells are not shown
      here to match adult human microglia in situ.
    divergences:
    - divergence_type: STRUCTURAL_IDEALIZATION
      description: >-
        The node places neuroinflammation in brain tissue where microglia,
        astrocytes and neurons interact. Here the interaction is reduced to
        one-way medium transfer between two monocultures, which is what makes
        the TNF-alpha dependence demonstrable but removes feedback.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    - divergence_type: CAUSE_UNREPRESENTED
      description: >-
        Activation is driven by TLR agonists and exogenous cytokines. Stress,
        the node's upstream route in this entry, is absent.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    readouts:
    - name: Stimulus- and time-dependent cytokine secretion profile
      target: Neuroinflammation
      direction: ALTERED
      interpretation: >-
        Establishes that the model reports distinguishable activation states
        rather than a single on-off response.
      evidence:
      - reference: PMID:41227333
        reference_title: Differential Responses of Human iPSC-Derived Microglia to Stimulation with Diverse Inflammogens.
        supports: SUPPORT
        evidence_source: IN_VITRO
        directness: DIRECT
        quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
        snippet: MGLCs displayed distinct morphologies and produced stimulus- and time-dependent cytokine secretion profiles upon exposure to diverse inflammatory stimuli
        explanation: >-
          The result itself: secretion profiles that differ by stimulus and by
          time, which is what makes this readout report distinguishable
          activation states rather than one on-off response.
    - name: Astrocytic NF-kB translocation after microglial supernatant transfer
      target: Neuroinflammation
      direction: INCREASED
      interpretation: >-
        A human-cell counterpart to the microglia-to-astrocyte propagation the
        entry already curates in mouse, with a soluble mediator identified by
        dependency.
      evidence:
      - reference: PMID:41227333
        reference_title: Differential Responses of Human iPSC-Derived Microglia to Stimulation with Diverse Inflammogens.
        supports: SUPPORT
        evidence_source: IN_VITRO
        directness: DIRECT
        quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
        snippet: MGLCs stimulated with FSL-1, LPS, or Poly(I:C) indirectly activated astrocytes via a strictly TNFα-dependent mechanism, highlighting the role of soluble mediators in the signal propagation.
        explanation: >-
          The result the readout records: astrocytes were activated, and the
          mediator was identified by dependency rather than inferred.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:41227333
      reference_title: Differential Responses of Human iPSC-Derived Microglia to Stimulation with Diverse Inflammogens.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: Altogether, this platform enables a dissection of microglia activation states and multi-parametric characterization of subsequent neuroinflammation.
      explanation: >-
        The authors' own statement of what the platform measures, which is
        what makes it a MEASURES link rather than a claim about the node.
    - reference: PMID:41227333
      reference_title: Differential Responses of Human iPSC-Derived Microglia to Stimulation with Diverse Inflammogens.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: Here, we generated microglia-like cells (MGLCs) from human induced pluripotent stem cells and characterized them as a robust, accessible model system for studying inflammatory activation.
      explanation: >-
        States what the system is and what it was built for.
  notes: >-
    Added from the alternative-models deep research run for this entry
    (research/Major_Depressive_Disorder-alternative-models-deep-research-openscientist.md).
    First experimental_models entry on this record.
- name: COiMg microglia-containing cerebral organoid
  experimental_model_type: ORGANOID
  organism:
    preferred_term: Homo sapiens
    term:
      id: NCBITaxon:9606
      label: Homo sapiens
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: Microglia
    term:
      id: CL:0000129
      label: microglial cell
  - preferred_term: Neuron
    term:
      id: CL:0000540
      label: neuron
  cell_source: Human induced pluripotent stem cells, with microglia integrated into cerebral organoids
  culture_system: Cerebral organoids with and without integrated microglia, compared side by side
  conditions:
  - Unstimulated
  - Interferon-gamma
  - Inflammatory stimuli
  publication: PMID:39500415
  description: >-
    Cerebral organoids with microglia integrated into them, built to study
    prenatal immune challenge. The organoids express microglial markers and
    respond to inflammatory stimuli. Microglial presence alters organoid
    development itself - cell density, neural differentiation, and ciliated and
    mesenchymal marker expression - and organoids with and without microglia
    respond to inflammatory stimuli both similarly and distinctly.
    Interferon-gamma produced transcriptional and structural change that
    depended on microglia being present, including altered expression of
    autism-linked genes.
  modeled_mechanisms:
  - target: Neuroinflammation
    relationship: PERTURBS
    fidelity: MODERATE
    model_scale: TISSUE
    description: >-
      Applies an inflammatory challenge to human brain tissue containing both
      microglia and neurons, and isolates the microglial contribution by
      comparing organoids that have them against ones that do not. That
      comparison is the model's distinctive capability and is not available in
      the entry's other models for this node.
    limitations: >-
      The study is about prenatal immune challenge and neurodevelopmental
      disorder risk, not depression; its outcome genes are autism-linked. The
      organoid is a developing cortical tissue with no hippocampal
      specification, no vasculature and no adaptive immune input, and the
      challenge is a single cytokine rather than chronic stress.
    divergences:
    - divergence_type: TEMPORAL_SCOPE
      description: >-
        The model is a fetal-stage developing tissue and the challenge is
        prenatal. The node concerns inflammation in an adult brain, so the
        developmental window in which the effect is read has no counterpart in
        the node.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    - divergence_type: POPULATION_MISMATCH
      description: >-
        Outcomes were framed and interpreted against neurodevelopmental
        disorder risk, autism in particular. Nothing in the study is
        depression-specific, so the model is being repurposed.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    - divergence_type: BOUNDARY_OMISSION
      description: >-
        No hippocampal identity, no blood-brain barrier and no peripheral
        immune compartment, so neither the node's anatomical locus nor the
        route by which peripheral inflammation is thought to reach the brain
        is represented.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    readouts:
    - name: Microglia-dependent transcriptional and structural change under interferon-gamma
      target: Neuroinflammation
      direction: ALTERED
      interpretation: >-
        Shows the cytokine response of the tissue requires microglia, which is
        the mechanistic claim the node makes about the cell type.
      evidence:
      - reference: PMID:39500415
        reference_title: A microglia-containing cerebral organoid model to study early life immune challenges.
        supports: SUPPORT
        evidence_source: IN_VITRO
        directness: DIRECT
        quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
        snippet: Additionally, IFN-γ induced significant transcriptional and structural changes in the cerebral organoids, that appear to be regulated by the presence of microglia.
        explanation: >-
          The microglia-dependence of the cytokine response, stated as a
          result.
    - name: Effect of microglial presence on organoid cell density and neural differentiation
      target: Neuroinflammation
      direction: ALTERED
      interpretation: >-
        A baseline, not an inflammatory, effect: microglia shape the tissue
        before any challenge, which constrains how the challenged condition is
        read.
      evidence:
      - reference: PMID:39500415
        reference_title: A microglia-containing cerebral organoid model to study early life immune challenges.
        supports: SUPPORT
        evidence_source: IN_VITRO
        directness: DIRECT
        quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
        snippet: The presence of microglia influences cerebral organoid development, including cell density and neural differentiation, and regulates the expression of several ciliated and mesenchymal cell markers.
        explanation: >-
          Records the confound in the with-versus-without comparison the model
          depends on.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39500415
      reference_title: A microglia-containing cerebral organoid model to study early life immune challenges.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: Here, we characterized a model of cerebral organoids (CO) with integrated microglia (COiMg). These organoids express typical microglial markers and respond to inflammatory stimuli.
      explanation: >-
        Defines the system and establishes that it is inflammation-responsive.
  notes: >-
    Added from the alternative-models deep research run for this entry.
    Included for the capability rather than the disease framing: the
    with-and-without-microglia comparison in human tissue is what no other
    model on this node offers. The autism and prenatal framing is recorded as
    a POPULATION_MISMATCH divergence so the record cannot be read as a
    depression organoid.
- name: HT-22 hippocampal cell line, corticosterone induction of Klf9
  experimental_model_type: CELL_LINE
  organism:
    preferred_term: Mus musculus
    term:
      id: NCBITaxon:10090
      label: Mus musculus
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: Hippocampal neuronal cell line
    description: >-
      Bound to the generic neuron term, not to CL:0002608 hippocampal neuron.
      HT-22 is an immortalised line derived from mouse hippocampus; binding
      the primary cell type would assert an identity the line does not have.
    term:
      id: CL:0000540
      label: neuron
  cell_source: HT-22 mouse hippocampal cell line
  culture_system: Cell line monolayer under corticosterone treatment, with protein synthesis inhibition, enhancer-reporter, gel shift and chromatin immunoprecipitation assays
  conditions:
  - Corticosterone, time course
  - Corticosterone, dose response
  - Corticosterone with protein synthesis inhibition
  publication: PMID:22962255
  description: >-
    The mouse hippocampal line HT-22 treated with corticosterone, used to
    establish how glucocorticoid drives Krueppel-like factor 9. Induction was
    time- and dose-dependent and survived protein synthesis inhibition,
    marking Klf9 as a direct glucocorticoid-response gene. Two GR/MR response
    elements were located at -6.1 and -5.3 kb and verified by
    enhancer-reporter, gel shift and chromatin immunoprecipitation; GR
    recruitment, histone hyperacetylation and nucleosome removal were seen at
    those regions. The -5.3 kb element is largely conserved across tetrapods,
    while orthologs of the -6.1 kb element were detected only in therian
    mammals.
  modeled_mechanisms:
  - target: Stress-Responsive Transcription Factor Reprogramming
    relationship: PERTURBS
    fidelity: MODERATE
    model_scale: MOLECULAR
    description: >-
      Manipulates the exact step the node names: corticosteroid control of
      KLF9 in hippocampal neurons. It establishes the regulation as direct and
      maps the cis-elements and the chromatin events through which it acts,
      which is the mechanism the node's footprinting data can only infer.
    limitations: >-
      An immortalised mouse line, so cell identity, chromatin state and
      ploidy are not those of human hippocampal neurons, and the node's
      cell-type resolution - granule cells, CA1-4 excitatory neurons, PENK+
      inhibitory neurons - cannot be represented at all. KLF15, EGR and ASCL1,
      also named in the node, are not addressed. The node describes altered
      transcription-factor binding activity in disease; this model shows
      normal hormonal regulation of one factor.
    divergences:
    - divergence_type: SPECIES_MISMATCH
      description: >-
        Mouse line standing in for human hippocampus, and the paper itself
        bounds the extrapolation: the -5.3 kb GR/MR element is largely
        conserved across tetrapods, but the -6.1 kb element was found only in
        therian mammals, so the two-element architecture is not a general
        vertebrate one.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    - divergence_type: STRUCTURAL_IDEALIZATION
      description: >-
        A homogeneous cell line replaces the cell-type-resolved human data the
        node is built from. There is no way to ask in this system whether
        KLF9 regulation differs between granule cells and PENK+ inhibitory
        neurons, which is the node's substance.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    - divergence_type: CONTESTED_ASSUMPTION
      description: >-
        The node is about reprogrammed, disease-associated binding activity.
        This model demonstrates intact physiological induction, so it supplies
        the mechanism that could be reprogrammed rather than evidence of
        reprogramming.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    readouts:
    - name: Klf9 mRNA after corticosterone treatment
      target: Stress-Responsive Transcription Factor Reprogramming
      direction: INCREASED
      interpretation: >-
        Direct glucocorticoid induction of one of the transcription factors
        the node names, in hippocampal cells.
      evidence:
      - reference: PMID:22962255
        reference_title: Molecular basis for glucocorticoid induction of the Kruppel-like factor 9 gene in hippocampal neurons.
        supports: SUPPORT
        evidence_source: IN_VITRO
        directness: DIRECT
        quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
        snippet: Treatment of the mouse hippocampal cell line HT-22 with CORT caused a time- and dose-dependent increase in Klf9 mRNA.
        explanation: >-
          The induction itself, with the two dependencies that make it a
          usable assay.
      - reference: PMID:22962255
        reference_title: Molecular basis for glucocorticoid induction of the Kruppel-like factor 9 gene in hippocampal neurons.
        supports: SUPPORT
        evidence_source: IN_VITRO
        directness: DIRECT
        quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
        snippet: The CORT induction of Klf9 was resistant to protein synthesis inhibition, suggesting that Klf9 is a direct CORT-response gene.
        explanation: >-
          Establishes directness, which is what separates this from a
          downstream correlation.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:22962255
      reference_title: Molecular basis for glucocorticoid induction of the Kruppel-like factor 9 gene in hippocampal neurons.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: Our findings support a predominant role for GR, with a minor contribution of MR, in the direct regulation of Klf9 acting via two GRE/MRE located in the 5'-flanking region of the gene.
      explanation: >-
        The paper's conclusion, including the receptor split, which matters
        because the entry's HPA node runs through the same two receptors.
  notes: >-
    Added from the alternative-models deep research run for this entry. The
    node also names KLF15, EGR and ASCL1 family factors; this model covers
    KLF9 only. Its value is that it is the mechanistic account behind one of
    the node's footprinting observations, in the same tissue type.
- name: Primed quiescent neural stem cell culture with an interferon response signature
  experimental_model_type: PRIMARY_CELL_CULTURE
  organism:
    preferred_term: Mus musculus
    term:
      id: NCBITaxon:10090
      label: Mus musculus
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: Neural stem cell
    term:
      id: CL:0000047
      label: neural stem cell
  cell_source: Adult mouse neural stem cells
  culture_system: In vitro quiescence induction by BMP-4 or by combined BMP-4 and FGF-2, with engraftment into the adult subventricular zone for validation
  conditions:
  - BMP-4, dormant quiescence
  - BMP-4 with FGF-2, primed quiescence
  publication: PMID:33972529
  description: >-
    Adult mouse neural stem cells driven into two distinct quiescent states in
    culture: BMP-4 alone gives a dormant non-cycling state, while BMP-4 with
    FGF-2 gives a primed state poised to re-enter the cell cycle. The primed
    state is defined by high LRIG1 and CD9 together with an interferon
    response signature, and engrafts efficiently into the adult
    subventricular zone niche. LRIG1 is the functional gatekeeper: disrupting
    Lrig1 in subventricular zone stem cells in vivo increases proliferation,
    and LRIG1 works by letting EGFR protein accumulate while limiting its
    signalling.
  modeled_mechanisms:
  - target: Neurogenic Niche Interferon Signaling Activation
    relationship: MEASURES
    fidelity: LOW
    model_scale: CELLULAR
    description: >-
      Puts an interferon response signature and a defined neural-stem-cell
      quiescence state in the same cells, which is the pairing the node
      asserts from human post-mortem data. It makes the association
      manipulable: quiescence state here is set experimentally rather than
      observed.
    limitations: >-
      In this system the interferon signature is a marker of a normal primed
      quiescent state, not a disease-associated activation, so the model
      supplies the association without the pathology. It is mouse
      subventricular zone, not human hippocampus, and the node's specific
      genes (EIF2AK2, IFIT3, HERC6, NRIR, IFITM3, MX1) are not the ones
      reported here. NRIR has no mouse ortholog, being a human long
      non-coding RNA. The node also records the interferon programme as raised
      in mature granule cells and CA1-4 excitatory neurons, which this model
      does not contain.
    divergences:
    - divergence_type: CONTESTED_ASSUMPTION
      description: >-
        The node treats raised interferon signalling in early neurogenic
        stages as a disease-associated change. Here the same signature marks a
        physiological primed quiescent state in healthy cells, which raises
        the possibility that the human signal reports a shift in stem-cell
        state rather than an inflammatory insult. That is a hypothesis this
        model makes testable, not a finding.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    - divergence_type: POPULATION_MISMATCH
      description: >-
        Mouse subventricular zone stem cells stand in for the human
        hippocampal neurogenic niche. Adult hippocampal neurogenesis in humans
        is itself contested, and the subventricular zone is a different niche
        with a different output.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    - divergence_type: BOUNDARY_OMISSION
      description: >-
        Cultured stem cells with no microglia, vasculature or mature neurons,
        so no source of interferon other than the cells themselves, and no way
        to test the hippocampus-wide spread of the programme that the node
        records.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    readouts:
    - name: Interferon response signature in primed quiescent neural stem cells
      target: Neurogenic Niche Interferon Signaling Activation
      direction: INCREASED
      interpretation: >-
        Associates the interferon programme with a specific, experimentally
        set stem-cell state. In healthy mouse cells, so it reports on the
        node's association rather than on its pathology.
      evidence:
      - reference: PMID:33972529
        reference_title: LRIG1 is a gatekeeper to exit from quiescence in adult neural stem cells.
        supports: SUPPORT
        evidence_source: IN_VITRO
        directness: INDIRECT
        quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
        snippet: Primed quiescent NSCs (p-qNSCs) are defined by high levels of LRIG1 and CD9, as well as an interferon response signature, and can efficiently engraft into the adult subventricular zone (SVZ) niche.
        explanation: >-
          The interferon signature as a defining feature of the primed
          quiescent state, in cells that are otherwise normal.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:33972529
      reference_title: LRIG1 is a gatekeeper to exit from quiescence in adult neural stem cells.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: IN_VITRO
      directness: DIRECT
      quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
      snippet: We show that BMP-4 signaling induces a dormant non-cycling quiescent state (d-qNSCs), whereas combined BMP-4/FGF-2 signaling induces a distinct primed quiescent state poised for cell cycle re-entry.
      explanation: >-
        How the two quiescent states are produced, which is what makes the
        association manipulable.
  notes: >-
    Added from the alternative-models deep research run for this entry. This
    model also bears on Stalled Adult Hippocampal Neurogenesis, which is a
    separate node on this record; the link is deliberately not asserted
    because the cells are subventricular zone rather than hippocampal and the
    node is about a stall rather than about quiescence state. The
    CONTESTED_ASSUMPTION divergence is the reason to keep the record: it names
    an alternative reading of the human interferon signal.
- name: Rat neostriatal slice culture, proenkephalin gene regulation
  experimental_model_type: OTHER
  organism:
    preferred_term: Rattus norvegicus
    term:
      id: NCBITaxon:10116
      label: Rattus norvegicus
  cell_types:
  - preferred_term: Medium spiny GABAergic projection neuron
    term:
      id: CL:1001474
      label: medium spiny neuron
  cell_source: Rat neostriatum
  culture_system: Organotypic slice culture
  conditions:
  - NMDA receptor stimulation
  - GABA-A receptor manipulation
  publication: PMID:11982623
  description: >-
    Organotypic slice cultures of rat neostriatum used to work out what
    controls proenkephalin gene expression. In the neostriatum the gene is
    expressed in medium spiny GABA neurons projecting to the globus pallidus,
    and its expression is driven by glutamatergic input through NMDA
    receptors. The cultures showed that GABA released from neostriatal neurons
    negatively regulates NMDA-driven proenkephalin expression, that the GABA-A
    receptors responsible appear to be colocalised with NMDA receptors on the
    same projection neurons, and that intrinsic striatal and thalamic
    glutamatergic afferents drive the gene as well as cortical ones.
  modeled_mechanisms:
  - target: PENK+ GABAergic Interneuron Activation
    relationship: MEASURES
    fidelity: LOW
    model_scale: MOLECULAR
    description: >-
      Informative by analogy only. It is the available experimental handle on
      what turns proenkephalin transcription up and down in a GABAergic
      neuron, and it identifies the controlling inputs - NMDA receptor drive,
      opposed by GABA-A signalling on the same cells. The node's population
      overexpresses proenkephalin alongside immediate-early genes in what the
      authors read as an activated state, and NMDA-driven activation opposed
      by local inhibition is a candidate mechanism for that. The cell the node
      names is not present in this system.
    limitations: >-
      Wrong cell, wrong region, wrong species. The node's population is a
      PENK+ medium-spiny-neuron-like GABAergic interneuron in human
      hippocampus, not previously described there; this is a GABAergic
      projection neuron in rat neostriatum. PENK+ medium spiny neurons are
      well described in rodent striatum, and that resemblance is what licenses
      the analogy at all; what the search behind this record did not find is a
      report of a hippocampal PENK+ interneuron population in a model species.
      So the model cannot recapitulate the node under any reading. It is
      recorded as the proenkephalin regulatory precedent, and should not be
      cited as a model of the node.
    divergences:
    - divergence_type: POPULATION_MISMATCH
      description: >-
        The node's cell is a hippocampal interneuron. This is a striatal
        projection neuron. The resemblance that licenses the analogy is that
        the node's population is described as medium-spiny-neuron-like and
        expresses proenkephalin, which is exactly the striatal phenotype, but
        a projection neuron and an interneuron are different cells with
        different circuit roles.
      materiality: INVALIDATING
    - divergence_type: SPECIES_MISMATCH
      description: >-
        Rat. The node's population was identified in human hippocampus and
        reported as not previously described there, so there is no established
        rat counterpart to appeal to.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    - divergence_type: STRUCTURAL_IDEALIZATION
      description: >-
        A slice culture retains local circuitry but is severed from the
        cortical, thalamic and stress-axis inputs that would make the node's
        activated state arise. Afferent drive is applied by the
        experimenter.
      materiality: QUALIFYING
    readouts:
    - name: NMDA-driven proenkephalin gene expression under endogenous GABA
      target: PENK+ GABAergic Interneuron Activation
      direction: DECREASED
      interpretation: >-
        Identifies a brake on proenkephalin transcription in a GABAergic
        neuron. Mechanistically suggestive for the node; in a different cell
        type and region.
      evidence:
      - reference: PMID:11982623
        reference_title: Intrinsic GABA neurons inhibit proenkephalin gene expression in slice cultures of rat neostriatum.
        supports: SUPPORT
        evidence_source: IN_VITRO
        directness: INDIRECT
        quote_role: PRIMARY_RESULT
        snippet: Our results show that GABA is released from neostriatal neurons and negatively regulates the proenkephalin gene expression induced by NMDA receptor stimulation.
        explanation: >-
          The regulatory relationship, which is what the analogy rests on.
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:11982623
      reference_title: Intrinsic GABA neurons inhibit proenkephalin gene expression in slice cultures of rat neostriatum.
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
      directness: INDIRECT
      quote_role: BACKGROUND
      snippet: In the neostriatum, the proenkephalin gene is expressed in medium spiny GABA neurons, which project to the globus pallidus.
      explanation: >-
        Establishes the cell type studied, and so the exact mismatch with the
        node's population. MODEL_ORGANISM because the quote states rat in vivo
        neuroanatomy from the paper's introduction, not a slice-culture
        result; BACKGROUND records that it is not a finding of this study.
  notes: >-
    Added from the alternative-models deep research run for this entry, and
    kept deliberately as informative by analogy only rather than dropped. No
    PENK-expressing medium-spiny-neuron-like population outside human
    hippocampus was found in a search for one; that search yielded this
    striatal regulatory work instead. The INVALIDATING POPULATION_MISMATCH
    divergence is the finding: no model is linked to this node that contains
    its cell type. Two other candidates were declined - PMID:35269475, an
    LHX6 reporter line that never mentions PENK, and PMID:40364981, a methods
    protocol with no result bearing on the node.

    cell_types is bound to CL:1001474 medium spiny neuron rather than to
    CL:4023029 indirect pathway medium spiny neuron. The cited abstract says
    the proenkephalin-expressing cells "project to the globus pallidus",
    which is consistent with the indirect pathway, but CL:4023029 is
    additionally defined by selective DRD2 expression, which this paper does
    not report. The parent term is what the source supports.

diagnosis:
- name: PHQ-9 depression screening and severity grading
  description: >-
    The Patient Health Questionnaire 9-item depression module (PHQ-9) is a
    self-report instrument used both to make criteria-based depression
    diagnoses and to grade depression severity. Its panel code identifies the
    instrument and its total-score code carries the published severity cut
    points.
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: depression screening
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15419
      label: Disease Screening
  measurements:
  - preferred_term: PHQ-9
    term:
      id: LOINC:44249-1
      label: PHQ-9 quick depression assessment panel [Reported.PHQ]
  reference_ranges:
  - loinc_term:
      id: LOINC:44261-6
      label: Patient Health Questionnaire 9 item (PHQ-9) total score [Reported]
    unit: '{score}'
    population: >-
      PHQ-9 validation sample, 8 primary care clinics and 7
      obstetrics-gynecology clinics (Kroenke 2001)
    notes: >-
      The source states the thresholds as "PHQ-9 scores of 5, 10, 15, and 20
      represented mild, moderate, moderately severe, and severe depression,
      respectively", and in its discussion as thresholds "demarcating the lower
      limits" of those categories, so each cut point is the inclusive lower
      bound of its band. The score range of 0 to 27 is stated in the same full
      text. The band below 5 carries no source label; it is named here by its
      interval (the paper reports likelihood ratios for scores of 0-4). The
      moderately severe band has no severity value because the band severity
      scale has only mild, moderate and severe. The same abstract reports that a
      score of 10 or more had a sensitivity of 88% and a specificity of 88% for
      major depression, which coincides with the lower bound of the moderate
      band.
    interpretation_bands:
    - name: Below the mild threshold (0-4)
      lower_bound: 0
      upper_bound: 5
      unit: '{score}'
      abnormal_flag: NORMAL
    - name: Mild depression
      lower_bound: 5
      upper_bound: 10
      unit: '{score}'
      abnormal_flag: HIGH
      severity: MILD
    - name: Moderate depression
      lower_bound: 10
      upper_bound: 15
      unit: '{score}'
      abnormal_flag: HIGH
      severity: MODERATE
    - name: Moderately severe depression
      lower_bound: 15
      upper_bound: 20
      unit: '{score}'
      abnormal_flag: HIGH
    - name: Severe depression
      lower_bound: 20
      upper_bound: 28
      unit: '{score}'
      abnormal_flag: HIGH
      severity: SEVERE
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:11556941
      reference_title: "The PHQ-9: validity of a brief depression severity measure."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        PHQ-9 scores of 5, 10, 15, and 20 represented mild, moderate,
        moderately severe, and severe depression, respectively.
      explanation: >-
        States the four severity cut points recorded as the band boundaries.
    - reference: PMID:11556941
      reference_title: "The PHQ-9: validity of a brief depression severity measure."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        PHQ-9 scores of 5, 10, 15, and 20 represent valid and easy-to-remember
        thresholds demarcating the lower limits of mild, moderate, moderately
        severe, and severe depression.
      explanation: >-
        Establishes that each cut point is the lower limit of its category,
        which is why each is recorded as an inclusive lower bound.
    - reference: PMID:11556941
      reference_title: "The PHQ-9: validity of a brief depression severity measure."
      supports: SUPPORT
      evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
      snippet: >-
        As a severity measure, the PHQ-9 score can range from 0 to 27
      explanation: >-
        Gives the score range that bounds the lowest and highest bands.
  notes: >-
    Copyright © Pfizer Inc. All rights reserved. Developed by Drs. Robert L.
    Spitzer, Janet B.W. Williams, Kurt Kroenke and colleagues, with an
    educational grant from Pfizer Inc. No permission required to reproduce,
    translate, display or distribute.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:11556941
    reference_title: "The PHQ-9: validity of a brief depression severity measure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In addition to making criteria-based diagnoses of depressive disorders,
      the PHQ-9 is also a reliable and valid measure of depression severity.
    explanation: >-
      The validation study's conclusion that the PHQ-9 serves both for
      depression diagnosis and for severity grading, the two uses this row
      records.
  - reference: PMID:11556941
    reference_title: "The PHQ-9: validity of a brief depression severity measure."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Using the MHP reinterview as the criterion standard, a PHQ-9 score ≥10
      had a sensitivity of 88% and a specificity of 88% for major depression.
    explanation: >-
      Criterion validity of the PHQ-9 against a structured mental health
      professional interview for major depression.

    - name: Severe depression

      explanation: >-
        States the Turkish-population severity cut-offs recorded as the band

  notes: >-

    The Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS) is a self-rating depression screening
    scale designed for older adults. The 30-item version is bound here by its
    panel code; no total-score code is bound because no cut-off is recorded.
  diagnosis_term:
    preferred_term: depression screening
    term:
      id: NCIT:C15419
      label: Disease Screening
  measurements:
  - preferred_term: GDS (30-item)
    term:
      id: LOINC:48542-5
      label: Geriatric depression scale (GDS) panel
  notes: >-
    No reference range is recorded because no cached source states a GDS
    cut-off in quotable text. The development paper (PMID:7183759, abstract
    only) classifies subjects as normal, mildly depressed or severely depressed
    without giving score boundaries, and the systematic reviews PMID:17087788,
    PMID:19800132 and PMID:31881393 (abstracts) report pooled sensitivity and
    specificity for the 30- and 15-item versions without naming the cut-off.
    A PubMed search for GDS papers stating "10-19" or "20-30" bands returned
    two studies that apply the scale rather than validate it, and a search for
    a GDS-30 cut-off of 10 or 11 stated in the abstract returned nothing. The
    GDS panel code carries no third-party
    copyright notice in the LOINC table. The 15-item short version has its own
    LOINC panel and total codes and is not bound here.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:7183759
    reference_title: "Development and validation of a geriatric depression screening scale: a preliminary report."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The authors suggest that the GDS represents a reliable and valid
      self-rating depression screening scale for elderly populations.
    explanation: >-
      The development and validation study of the GDS supports its use for
      depression screening in older adults.
  - reference: PMID:19800132
    reference_title: "Diagnostic validity and added value of the Geriatric Depression Scale for depression in primary care: a meta-analysis of GDS30 and GDS15."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    quote_role: REVIEW_SYNTHESIS
    snippet: >-
      Diagnostic accuracy of the GDS(30) after meta-analytic weighting was
      given by a sensitivity of 77.4% (95% CI=66.3% to 86.8%) and a
      specificity=65.4% (95% CI=44.2% to 83.8%).
    explanation: >-
      Pooled diagnostic accuracy of the 30-item GDS against psychiatric
      interview in primary care.
discussions:
- discussion_id: gap_mdd_fgf13_jip2_jnk_human_validity
  prompt: >-
    Does the FGF13-MAPK8IP2/JIP2-JNK-BAX/BCL2 apoptosis chain operate
    endogenously in adult human astrocytes in MDD, or is the reported phenotype
    specific to a stress model, developmental culture, brain region, sex, or a
    different JIP2-linked kinase? If astrocyte loss occurs, is this chain a
    causal driver of neuroinflammation and synaptic dysfunction, a downstream
    amplifier, or one of several cell-death programs?
  kind: HUMAN_MODEL_MISMATCH
  status: OPEN
  attaches_to:
  - mechanistic_hypotheses#astrocytic_fgf13_jip2_jnk_cell_death_model
  - pathophysiology#Neuroinflammation
  - pathophysiology#Neuroplasticity Deficits
  - animal_models#Astrocyte-specific Fgf13 knockout and overexpression mouse under chronic stress
  rationale: >-
    The seed study provides bidirectional astrocyte-specific Fgf13 perturbation
    in chronic-restraint- and social-defeat-stress male mice and pathway
    readouts in neonatal primary mouse astrocytes. Its human component is
    instead a secondary reanalysis of GSE144136: all 17 MDD donors were male,
    died by suicide, and contributed dorsolateral prefrontal cortex rather than
    hippocampus. It neither demonstrates astrocyte death nor measures FGF13
    protein, JIP2 activity, phospho-JNK, or BAX/BCL2 target engagement in the
    same adult human cells. The original dataset emphasized excitatory neurons
    and oligodendrocyte precursor cells. A 2024 mini-review describes FGF13 as
    prominently expressed in developing and mature central and peripheral
    neurons, so the context-specific astrocytic source premise is itself
    single-sourced to the seed study and requires independent cell-type
    localization. Human hippocampal findings are
    region-, marker-, treatment-, and sex-dependent: studies report no major
    cell-death morphology, increased nonspecific glial packing density, or
    decreased hilar GFAP-immunoreactive astrocyte density only in unmedicated
    MDD, with female-specific GFAP area-fraction changes. An independent
    bulk-frontal-cortex study also found transcript-specific FGF-system
    dysregulation across MDD cohorts but did not resolve astrocytes. A separate
    both-sex dlPFC single-nucleus study found broadly similar threshold-free
    expression patterns but different significant DEG contributors, with
    astrocytes among the major male contributors; this supports sex-stratified
    validation but not an FGF13-specific or male-only inference. In male
    stress-exposed mice, astrocyte-specific Fgf2 manipulation also altered
    social avoidance through a distinct neurovascular/BBB route, showing that
    astrocytic FGF and behavioral endpoints are not specific to the FGF13-JIP2
    chain. A second FGF-family result runs in the opposite direction:
    hippocampal FGF9 transcript is elevated in postmortem MDD and reciprocal to
    FGF2, and bidirectional rodent FGF9 manipulation moves negative affect, so
    the sign of the FGF change that accompanies depression depends on which
    family member is measured and is not settled by an FGF13 loss model.
    Other stress-mouse studies implicate NLRP3-caspase-1-GSDMD pyroptosis
    or microglial IL-6/astrocyte IL-6R signaling, and earlier FHF-IB2
    biochemistry favored p38delta rather than JNK. Human relevance, cell-death
    identity, kinase specificity, and causal position therefore remain
    unresolved; clinical targeting would be premature.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:42421017
    reference_title: "FGF13 alleviates astrocytic apoptosis via JIP2 inhibition in the hippocampus and mitigates depression-like behavior."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: >-
      Astrocyte-specific knockout of FGF13 induces astrocytic apoptosis,
      exacerbates inflammatory levels, and aggravates depression-like behaviors
      in mice.
    explanation: >-
      Establishes the mouse causal evidence whose fidelity to adult human MDD
      astrocytes is the central mismatch.
  - reference: PMID:39332965
    reference_title: "Fibroblast Growth Factor (FGF) 13."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: OTHER
    snippet: >-
      Similar to other FHFs, FGF13 has been considered a non-secreted protein
      that lacks an amino signal and is prominently expressed in developing and
      mature neurons of the central and peripheral nervous systems, as well as
      the heart.
    explanation: >-
      This mini-review provides canonical expression context rather than direct
      MDD evidence: prominent neuronal expression makes the seed study's
      astrocytic source premise independently unreplicated, while not excluding
      context-specific astrocytic expression.
  - reference: PMID:32341540
    reference_title: "Single-nucleus transcriptomics of the prefrontal cortex in major depressive disorder implicates oligodendrocyte precursor cells and excitatory neurons."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Here we used single-nucleus transcriptomics to examine ~80,000 nuclei from
      the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex of male individuals with MDD (n = 17)
      and of healthy controls (n = 17).
    explanation: >-
      Defines the sex-restricted, cross-sectional human dataset reused by the
      seed study; it cannot separate MDD from suicide or test hippocampal
      signaling and apoptosis.
  - reference: PMID:32341540
    reference_title: "Single-nucleus transcriptomics of the prefrontal cortex in major depressive disorder implicates oligodendrocyte precursor cells and excitatory neurons."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      We found that the greatest dysregulation occurred in deep layer
      excitatory neurons and immature oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs),
      and these contributed almost half (47%) of all changes in gene expression.
    explanation: >-
      The source dataset's dominant signals were not astrocytic, making the
      secondary FGF13 astrocyte association hypothesis-generating rather than
      pathway validation.
  - reference: PMID:15483108
    reference_title: "Dysregulation of the fibroblast growth factor system in major depression."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      In this report we describe findings that imply dysregulation of several
      fibroblast growth factor (FGF) system transcripts in frontal cortical
      regions of brains from human subjects with major depressive disorder
      (MDD). This altered gene expression was discovered by microarray analysis
      of frontal cortical tissue from MDD, bipolar, and nonpsychiatric control
      subjects and was verified by quantitative real-time PCR analysis and,
      importantly, in a separate cohort of MDD subjects.
    explanation: >-
      This independent bulk-frontal-cortex study provides transcript- and
      cohort-dependent human FGF-system context, but it did not resolve
      astrocytes and therefore neither validates the later cell-type-specific
      FGF13 association nor establishes JIP2-JNK activity or apoptosis.
  - reference: PMID:37217515
    reference_title: "Cell type specific transcriptomic differences in depression show similar patterns between males and females but implicate distinct cell types and genes."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      Cell type specific transcriptome-wide threshold-free MDD-associated gene
      expression patterns were similar between the sexes, but significant
      differentially expressed genes (DEGs) diverged. Among 7 broad cell types
      and 41 clusters evaluated, microglia and parvalbumin interneurons
      contributed the most DEGs in females, while deep layer excitatory neurons,
      astrocytes, and oligodendrocyte precursors were the major contributors in
      males.
    explanation: >-
      This both-sex dlPFC study supports testing sex-specific cell-type
      contributions, but its similar threshold-free patterns and different
      significant DEG contributors do not establish a male-only mechanism or
      implicate FGF13, JIP2, kinase activity, or astrocyte death.
  - reference: PMID:41545369
    reference_title: "Environmental enrichment and physical exercise prevent stress-induced social avoidance and blood-brain barrier alterations via Fgf2."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: >-
      Fgf2 is mostly expressed by glial cells, and viral-mediated
      astrocyte-specific Fgf2 upregulation prevents stress-induced social
      avoidance while downregulation increases stress susceptibility and blunts
      physical exercise benefits.
    explanation: >-
      Bidirectional astrocytic Fgf2 manipulation identifies a parallel
      stress-resilience route in male mice, centered on nucleus-accumbens
      neurovascular protection rather than FGF13-JIP2 signaling or astrocyte
      apoptosis. It makes shared behavioral and inflammatory endpoints
      non-specific without refuting the FGF13 model.
  - reference: PMID:26351673
    reference_title: "Fibroblast growth factor 9 is a novel modulator of negative affect."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      using three microarray analyses followed by quantitative RT-PCR
      confirmation, we show that FGF9 expression is up-regulated in the
      hippocampus of individuals with MDD, and that FGF9 expression is
      inversely related to the expression of FGF2
    explanation: >-
      An independent postmortem series localizes an FGF-system change to the
      MDD hippocampus, the region the seed mouse work implicates, but the
      change is an increase in a different family member and is reciprocal to
      FGF2. It is bulk tissue, so it assigns no cell type and measures neither
      JIP2, kinase activity, nor astrocyte death; it therefore neither supports
      nor refutes an astrocytic FGF13 loss.
  - reference: PMID:26351673
    reference_title: "Fibroblast growth factor 9 is a novel modulator of negative affect."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: >-
      Chronic intracerebroventricular administration of FGF9 increased both
      anxiety- and depression-like behaviors. In contrast, knocking down FGF9
      expression in the dentate gyrus of the hippocampus using a lentiviral
      vector produced a decrease in FGF9 expression and ameliorated
      anxiety-like behavior.
    explanation: >-
      Bidirectional rodent manipulation of hippocampal FGF9 moves the same
      affective endpoints the seed study attributes to astrocytic FGF13,
      establishing FGF9 as a parallel FGF-family route rather than a test of
      the FGF13-JIP2-JNK chain. Shared behavioral readouts across FGF family
      members are therefore not specific evidence for that chain.
  - reference: PMID:11860455
    reference_title: "Neither major depression nor glucocorticoid treatment affects the cellular integrity of the human hippocampus."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      There was no evidence of neuronal cell loss or other major morphological
      alterations in any of the groups, nor was there a significant change in
      the distribution pattern of synaptophysin or Alz-50.
    explanation: >-
      This small mixed postmortem cohort pooled 15 donors with major depression
      or bipolar affective disorder and did not use astrocyte-specific apoptosis
      markers. Its lack of major hippocampal morphological loss and finding of
      only regional GFAP changes argue against assuming generalized human
      hippocampal cell loss from stress-mouse data.
  - reference: PMID:15522247
    reference_title: "Cellular changes in the postmortem hippocampus in major depression."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The density of granule cells and glia in the dentate gyrus and pyramidal
      neurons and glia in all cornv ammonis (CA)/hippocampal subfields is
      significantly increased by 30%-35% in MDD.
    explanation: >-
      Direct stereological sampling found increased glial packing density, not
      demonstrated astrocyte apoptosis; the authors instead proposed reduced
      neuropil and differential tissue shrinkage, underscoring unresolved human
      histopathology.
  - reference: PMID:26742791
    reference_title: "Density of GFAP-immunoreactive astrocytes is decreased in left hippocampi in major depressive disorder."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: HUMAN_CLINICAL
    snippet: >-
      The density of astrocytes in the hilus, but not CA1 or CA2/3, was
      significantly decreased only in depressed subjects not taking an
      antidepressant drug, but not for depressed subjects taking an
      antidepressant drug. The area fraction of GFAP-immunoreactivity was
      significantly decreased in the dentate gyrus in women but not men with
      depression.
    explanation: >-
      This direct human MDD study supports a region-, medication-, and
      sex-qualified GFAP-immunoreactive astrocyte phenotype, but its
      cross-sectional marker-density result cannot distinguish apoptosis from
      marker loss or determine whether antidepressants prevented or restored
      the difference.
  - reference: PMID:34877938
    reference_title: "NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD-mediated pyroptosis exerts a crucial role in astrocyte pathological injury in mouse model of depression."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: >-
      Here, we observed that depressive mice showed astrocytic pyroptosis, which
      was responsible for astrocyte loss, and selective serotonin reuptake
      inhibitor (SSRI) treatment could attenuate the pyroptosis induced by the
      chronic mild stress (CMS) model.
    explanation: >-
      A genetically interrogated mouse study supports a competing or parallel
      astrocyte cell-death program that must be distinguished from
      FGF13-JIP2-JNK-mediated apoptosis.
  - reference: PMID:39888279
    reference_title: "Microglia-Derived Interleukin-6 Triggers Astrocyte Apoptosis in the Hippocampus and Mediates Depression-Like Behavior."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: MODEL_ORGANISM
    snippet: >-
      Subsequent studies demonstrate that IL-6 released from activated microglia
      promotes astrocyte apoptosis. Furthermore, the knockdown of the P2X7
      receptor (P2X7R) in microglia, which is implicated in the stress response,
      reduces stress-induced microglial activation, IL-6 release, and astrocyte
      apoptosis. Direct inhibition of microglia by minocycline corroborates
      these effects. The selective knockdown of IL-6 in microglia and IL-6
      receptors in astrocytes effectively mitigates depression-like behaviors
      and reduces astrocyte atrophy.
    explanation: >-
      Cell-type-selective epistasis in a social-defeat mouse model identifies a
      distinct upstream microglia-to-astrocyte apoptosis route; FGF13 could be
      downstream, parallel, or model-specific rather than the initiating lesion.
  - reference: PMID:12244047
    reference_title: "Fibroblast growth factor homologous factors and the islet brain-2 scaffold protein regulate activation of a stress-activated protein kinase."
    supports: SUPPORT
    evidence_source: IN_VITRO
    snippet: >-
      Mixed lineage kinase 3 (MLK3) and IB2 synergistically activate p38delta but
      not the MAPKs JNK-1 and p38alpha.
    explanation: >-
      This prior biochemical result makes JNK-versus-p38delta pathway
      discrimination and an interaction-deficient FGF13 rescue essential.
  proposed_experiments:
  - experiment_id: exp_mdd_fgf13_human_multiregion_validation
    name: Adult human multi-region astrocyte pathway and cell-fate validation
    description: >-
      In an independently powered postmortem cohort, jointly stratify MDD
      diagnosis and cause of death (MDD nonsuicide, MDD suicide, psychiatric
      suicide without MDD, and psychiatrically healthy nonsuicide controls),
      include both sexes, and sample dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, anterior
      cingulate cortex, and hippocampus from the same donors where possible.
      Combine astrocyte-resolved spatial or single-nucleus transcriptomics with
      RNAscope and multiplex protein/phosphoprotein imaging. Quantify FGF13
      isoforms, MAPK8IP2, phospho-JNK/c-Jun, phospho-p38delta, BAX/BCL2,
      cleaved-caspase-3/TUNEL, NLRP3/GSDMD, IL-6R, astrocyte abundance, and
      morphology. Pre-register region-by-sex tests and separate marker
      downregulation or atrophy from irreversible cell death.
    experiment_type:
      preferred_term: multi-region postmortem molecular pathology study
    model_systems:
    - name: Multi-region postmortem human MDD brain cohort
      description: >-
        Adult human brain tissue balanced across diagnosis, suicide status, and
        sex and matched on age, postmortem interval, tissue pH, medication
        exposure, illness duration, and agonal factors.
      experimental_model_type: OTHER
      organism:
        preferred_term: human
        term:
          id: NCBITaxon:9606
          label: Homo sapiens
      cell_types:
      - preferred_term: astrocyte
        term:
          id: CL:0000127
          label: astrocyte
    readouts:
    - name: Within-astrocyte FGF13-JIP2 stress-kinase state
      target: mechanistic_hypotheses#astrocytic_fgf13_jip2_jnk_cell_death_model
      description: >-
        Measure FGF13 isoform abundance, MAPK8IP2, phospho-JNK/c-Jun, and
        phospho-p38delta in spatially identified astrocytes in each region.
      assays:
      - preferred_term: spatial transcriptomics
      - preferred_term: multiplex immunofluorescence
    - name: Astrocyte fate and cell-death-mode assignment
      target: mechanistic_hypotheses#astrocytic_fgf13_jip2_jnk_cell_death_model
      description: >-
        Distinguish apoptosis, pyroptosis, reversible atrophy, marker loss, and
        true numerical depletion using orthogonal cell-fate and stereological
        measures.
      biological_processes:
      - preferred_term: apoptotic process
        term:
          id: GO:0006915
          label: apoptotic process
      - preferred_term: pyroptotic inflammatory response
        term:
          id: GO:0070269
          label: pyroptotic inflammatory response
      assays:
      - preferred_term: design-based stereology
      - preferred_term: terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling assay
    controls:
    - name: Diagnosis-by-suicide factorial controls
      description: >-
        MDD nonsuicide and non-MDD psychiatric suicide groups separate
        diagnosis-associated signals from suicide-associated signals.
    - name: Preanalytic and treatment matching
      description: >-
        Match or model age, sex, postmortem interval, tissue pH, agonal state,
        medication exposure, substance use, and illness duration.
    - name: Orthogonal astrocyte identity and fate controls
      description: >-
        Require multiple astrocyte markers plus stereology so reduced GFAP or
        RNA recovery is not misclassified as cell death.
    decision_criterion: >-
      Human relevance is supported only if an independent cohort shows
      co-occurring lower FGF13, JIP2-linked JNK activation, and apoptotic fate
      within the same adult astrocytes after adjustment for suicide,
      medication, preanalytic factors, region, and sex, with a prespecified
      replication region. A signal restricted to suicide, one sex or one
      cortical region supports a restricted modifier rather than generalized
      MDD pathophysiology. Absence or reversal of the within-cell chain, a
      p38delta- rather than JNK-linked state, or evidence for atrophy/marker loss
      without apoptosis weakens the hypothesis.
    would_support:
    - mechanistic_hypotheses#astrocytic_fgf13_jip2_jnk_cell_death_model
    would_refute:
    - mechanistic_hypotheses#astrocytic_fgf13_jip2_jnk_cell_death_model
  - experiment_id: exp_mdd_fgf13_jip2_cross_species_epistasis
    name: Human-astrocyte and adult-mouse FGF13-JIP2 kinase epistasis
    description: >-
      Run a preregistered, bidirectional epistasis matrix in sex-balanced human
      iPSC-derived astrocyte-neuron-microglia tricultures and in adult,
      inducible astrocyte-specific Fgf13 mice under stressed and unstressed
      conditions. Compare FGF13 loss with wild-type rescue, overexpression, and
      an interaction-deficient FGF13 rescue; cross these arms with MAPK8IP2
      loss/rescue and selective JNK-versus-p38delta perturbation. In parallel,
      block IL-6/IL-6R and NLRP3/GSDMD pathways to test whether they are
      upstream, downstream, or independent. Use blinded allocation and analysis,
      temporal sampling before cell loss, and mediation analysis linking
      astrocyte survival to inflammatory, synaptic, network, and behavioral
      outcomes.
    experiment_type:
      preferred_term: cross-species genetic epistasis and rescue experiment
    model_systems:
    - name: Human iPSC-derived astrocyte-neuron-microglia triculture
      description: >-
        Multiple male and female donor lines with isogenic edits, matured before
        glucocorticoid or inflammatory stress and sampled longitudinally.
      experimental_model_type: CO_CULTURE
      organism:
        preferred_term: human
        term:
          id: NCBITaxon:9606
          label: Homo sapiens
      cell_types:
      - preferred_term: astrocyte
        term:
          id: CL:0000127
          label: astrocyte
      - preferred_term: neuron
        term:
          id: CL:0000540
          label: neuron
      - preferred_term: microglial cell
        term:
          id: CL:0000129
          label: microglial cell
    - name: Adult inducible astrocyte-specific Fgf13 mouse
      description: >-
        Both-sex adult inducible loss- and gain-of-function cohorts tested with
        and without chronic restraint stress, plus a sex-appropriate
        social-defeat replication.
      experimental_model_type: OTHER
      organism:
        preferred_term: mouse
        term:
          id: NCBITaxon:10090
          label: Mus musculus
      cell_types:
      - preferred_term: astrocyte
        term:
          id: CL:0000127
          label: astrocyte
    perturbations:
    - name: Bidirectional FGF13 dosage and domain-specific rescue
      target: mechanistic_hypotheses#astrocytic_fgf13_jip2_jnk_cell_death_model
      genes:
      - preferred_term: FGF13
        term:
          id: hgnc:3670
          label: FGF13
      effect: loss, overexpression, wild-type rescue, and JIP2-binding-deficient rescue
    - name: MAPK8IP2 genetic epistasis
      target: mechanistic_hypotheses#astrocytic_fgf13_jip2_jnk_cell_death_model
      genes:
      - preferred_term: MAPK8IP2
        term:
          id: hgnc:6883
          label: MAPK8IP2
      effect: knockout or knockdown followed by wild-type scaffold rescue
    - name: JNK-versus-p38delta and alternative-death-pathway discrimination
      target: mechanistic_hypotheses#astrocytic_fgf13_jip2_jnk_cell_death_model
      description: >-
        Use orthogonal genetic and selective pharmacologic perturbations of JNK
        and p38delta, plus IL-6/IL-6R and NLRP3/GSDMD blockade, with biochemical
        target-engagement confirmation.
    readouts:
    - name: Temporal stress-kinase activation and astrocyte death mode
      target: mechanistic_hypotheses#astrocytic_fgf13_jip2_jnk_cell_death_model
      description: >-
        Quantify FGF13-JIP2 binding, JNK and p38delta activity, BAX/BCL2,
        caspase-dependent apoptosis, gasdermin-dependent pyroptosis, and
        lineage-traced astrocyte survival before and after stress.
      biological_processes:
      - preferred_term: apoptotic process
        term:
          id: GO:0006915
          label: apoptotic process
      - preferred_term: pyroptotic inflammatory response
        term:
          id: GO:0070269
          label: pyroptotic inflammatory response
      assays:
      - preferred_term: co-immunoprecipitation assay
      - preferred_term: live-cell lineage imaging
    - name: Inflammatory and synaptic mediation
      target: pathophysiology#Neuroinflammation
      description: >-
        Measure cytokine release, microglial state, synaptic-protein abundance,
        neuronal morphology, and multielectrode-array network function; test
        whether preventing astrocyte death mediates these downstream effects. In
        the mouse arms, also measure astrocytic Fgf2, endothelial Cldn5, and BBB
        permeability as a prespecified parallel neurovascular comparator.
      assays:
      - preferred_term: cytokine quantification
      - preferred_term: multielectrode array recording
      - preferred_term: blood-brain barrier permeability assay
    - name: Stress behavior with specificity controls
      target: pathophysiology#Neuroplasticity Deficits
      description: >-
        In mice, combine reward- and social-interaction measures with open-field
        locomotion, anxiety, pain sensitivity, and stress-hormone readouts so
        nonspecific performance changes are not called antidepressant effects.
      assays:
      - preferred_term: behavioral phenotyping
    controls:
    - name: Isogenic and vector controls
      description: >-
        Use sham-edited isogenic cultures, wild-type littermates, driver-only
        and vector-only mice, and matched unstressed arms.
    - name: Binding-deficient and pathway-specific rescue controls
      description: >-
        Compare wild-type FGF13 rescue with a biochemically verified
        JIP2-binding-deficient rescue and confirm target engagement for each
        kinase intervention.
    - name: Sex, maturation, allocation, and assay controls
      description: >-
        Balance sex and donor background, use mature rather than neonatal human
        astrocytes, randomize and blind mouse studies, and include locomotor and
        viability controls.
    decision_criterion: >-
      The proposed chain is supported only if FGF13 loss precedes astrocyte
      apoptosis in both systems; wild-type but not interaction-deficient FGF13
      rescues it; MAPK8IP2 loss and JNK-selective blockade abolish the
